# Subham Kumar

Subham Kumar is a full-stack developer building web and mobile applications with React, Next.js, React Native, Node.js, TypeScript, and related JavaScript technologies.

Written notes:
The notes section contains long-form technical explanations aimed at working
developers preparing for interviews. Each note explains a group of related
topics in plain English, includes diagrams, states the common mistakes that
cause real bugs, and gives a spoken-answer version suitable for an interview.
Notes end with self-test questions and coding exercises.

Topics covered in the notes so far:
- var, let and const, and the temporal dead zone
- Hoisting, and the difference between ReferenceError and TypeError
- Primitives versus objects, and why JavaScript is always pass by value
- Type coercion, == versus ===, and the eight falsy values
- typeof, instanceof and reliable type checking
- Destructuring, defaults and nested patterns
- Spread and rest, and why a spread copy is only one level deep
- Optional chaining, nullish coalescing, and why ?? beats || for user data
- Template literals and tagged templates
- Strict mode
- Floating point precision, and why 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3
- JSON.stringify and JSON.parse, and what they silently destroy
- Symbols and well-known symbols
- Labels, switch fallthrough and the comma operator
